report_name: Ransomware Groups Standardize EDR-Kill Tactics to Evade Defenses

threat_actors.name: The Gentlemen
threat_actors.description: A prominent ransomware group identified as systematically reverse-engineering and incorporating effective EDR-kill techniques from other ransomware families like Babuk, Qilin, and Medusa.
threat_actors.goals: To disable endpoint security and successfully deploy ransomware for financial gain.

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: One of the most active ransomware groups in Q2 2026, with 293 publicly claimed attacks. The group is noted for using EDR-kill techniques as part of its standard operating procedure.
threat_actors.goals: To disable endpoint security and successfully deploy ransomware for financial gain.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware groups use custom scripts or built-in tools to stop services and kill processes associated with EDR and antivirus products to evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors obtain elevated privileges to disable or modify security tools like EDR.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: After disabling defenses, ransomware groups proceed to encrypt data on victim systems.

attack_patterns.name: Debugger Evasion
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware groups like The Gentlemen reverse-engineer other malware, which informs the development of techniques like debugger evasion and advanced obfuscation.

attack_patterns.name: Generative AI
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors are increasingly using Artificial Intelligence not only for creating malware but also for assisting in victim negotiations.

indicators.name: EDR Process Termination via Taskkill
indicators.pattern:
title: EDR Process Termination via Taskkill
id: 2a8f1b9c-4e7d-4f6a-8c1b-9e2d3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of taskkill.exe to forcefully terminate a process, a common technique for disabling EDR agents.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-27
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ransomware-q2-2026-edr-kill/
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\taskkill.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/IM'
      - '/F'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the `taskkill` command with the `/F` (force) flag to terminate a process by its image name, a common method used by ransomware to disable EDR agents.

indicators.name: EDR Service Manipulation via SC
indicators.pattern:
title: EDR Service Manipulation via SC.exe
id: 3b9c2d0e-5f8e-4g7b-9d2c-0f3e4g5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to stop or disable a service using sc.exe, a technique used to disable EDR services.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-27
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ransomware-q2-2026-edr-kill/
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_stop:
    Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'stop'
  selection_disable:
    Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'config'
      - 'start= disabled'
  condition: 1 of them
indicators.description: Detects the use of `sc.exe` to either stop a service or configure it to be disabled, which are common tactics for disabling EDR agents.

indicators.name: Security Tool Termination Utilities
indicators.pattern:
title: Security Tool Termination Utilities Execution
id: 4c0d3e1f-6g9f-4h8c-ae3d-1g4f5h6c7d8e
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of legitimate but powerful process management tools often abused by attackers to terminate security software.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-27
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ransomware-q2-2026-edr-kill/
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\PCHunter.exe'
      - '\ProcessHacker.exe'
      - '\kdu.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of PCHunter, Process Hacker, or kdu.exe, which are tools known to be used by threat actors to forcefully terminate EDR and other security processes.

indicators.name: Filter Driver Unload via fltMC
indicators.pattern:
title: Filter Driver Unload via fltMC.exe
id: 5d1e4f2g-7h0g-4i9d-bf4e-2h5g6i7d8e9f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of fltMC.exe to unload a filter driver, a technique used to disable EDR and other security products.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-27
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/ransomware-q2-2026-edr-kill/
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\fltMC.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'unload'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the Windows Filter Manager Control Program (`fltMC.exe`) to unload a filter driver, which can be used to disable security software.
